chapter_title: Also concerning the Catechumen; shall he be saved in a single Body?
chapter_note: This chapter is overwhelmingly later institutional/pastoral instruction about catechumens (fasting, alms, church loyalty, forgiveness of sins), wrapped in dialogue and praise formulas. Only two short passages preserve older, impersonal cosmological-soteriological mechanics (post-mortem ascent/purification and the formation of the “light image”), embedded inside catechumen/church application and (once) an NT-style treasure saying.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Dialogue frame (“Once again… speaks… to this apostle”), catechumen topic; hagiographic apparatus rather than impersonal cosmological exposition.
Beseeching/question formula and explicit intent to instruct “my other brothers” and catechumens; community editorial frame.

Conduct-description of the ‘perfect catechumen’ (marriage/household/wealth detachment, heart set on the holy church). Even though it contains a speech attribution, the substance is institutional ethics, not cosmos→cosmos mapping.
Explicit ‘saviour’ + apostle citation of 1 Cor 7 language; entered via NT/Pauline tradition.
Seam-flagged editorial extension summarizing ‘perfect catechumens’ and equating them with elect; institutional vocabulary dominates.
Rules/virtues (fasting, prayer, alms, church attendance) plus ‘children/wife’ brought into church; institutional application throughout.
Exhortative identification (‘good pearl’, catechumens) and internal book reference; not an impersonal cosmological register.

paragraphs.core_text: When, however, they come forth from their body, they travel on their way and pass by in the place above, and go in to the life. They shall be purified in the heavens, and they are plucked just as a fruit that ripens is plucked from the tree.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the institutional/application analogy beginning “In just the same way, this alms-offering that passes over to the elect…” through “Similarly, the souls of the catechumens…” because it pivots from cosmological process to church practice (alms to elect) and catechumen-specific application.
paragraphs.temporal_note: The extracted lines are impersonal cosmological mechanics (post-mortem transit, heavenly purification) with a natural correspondence (ripe fruit plucked). The removed continuation applies the image to alms/elect/catechumens—crossing into institutional present.
Institutional bookkeeping (‘contribution to the church’) and deference to another manual (‘Treasure of Life’); not substrate.
Prescriptive repentance/forgiveness via ‘God and the holy church’ and accounting of sins; institutional soteriology.
Closing-praise scene with disciples blessing the teacher; hagiographic frame.
Question frame (‘we beseech you’) introducing a catechetical problem-list (idols, sects, magic, murder, etc.); community Q&A apparatus.

Though it contains cosmological terms (‘separated the light from the darkness’), the salvation logic is mediated by ‘right hand of peace’ from the Light Mind ‘who dwells in the holy church’—an ecclesial rite/context rather than substrate exposition.
Absolution doctrine tied to entry into faith away from ‘sects and idols’; moral/institutional discipline.
Warning against relapse; catechumen/elect state as church categories; not cosmological mapping.
Explicit catechumen instruction: absolution through fasting/prayer/alms.
Detailed rulekeeping (fifty fasts, sexual abstinence on lord’s days, dietary prohibitions); institutional discipline.
Hours of prayer, daily alms, ‘garment… upon the saints’, ‘daily communion’; church practice.
Merit accounting (‘five parts’, ‘protection of the holy church’, ‘faith and love of the elect’) even where cosmological phrases appear; application dominates.

paragraphs.core_text: ⟨p.234⟩ As for the rest, he shall be questioned about a single part; and receive blows for (those sins) and retribution. Afterwards he is purified, whether indeed above or below. He shall be purified according to the worth of his deeds, and cleansed and washed and adorned. Afterwards, he is sculpted a light image; and [he glid]es up and reaches the land of rest,
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the closing clause “so that the place where his heart is, his treasure also will be there.” It functions as a moralizing ‘treasure’ maxim (Mt 6-style) rather than the impersonal cosmological process of purification and ascent.
paragraphs.temporal_note: The extracted portion is process-description (purification, transformation into a ‘light image’, ascent to the ‘land of rest’) characteristic of older cosmological teaching, while the removed ending shifts to a Gospel-style ethical aphorism.
Conditional exhortation about steadfastness in catechumenate and recompense; institutional.
Moral warning against lying/apostasy and total sin reckoning; disciplinary tone.
Promise of ‘destiny’ and salvation conditioned on steadfast faith; hortatory soteriology rather than systematic cosmology.
Narrative closure/praise (‘these disciples… gave glory’); although it names ‘the first light’ and ‘the Mind’, its voice is doxological frame, not substrate exposition.
